title: Essential and Potentially Toxic Elements in Commercial Milk Formulas: Health Risk Assessment Through a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
authors: Largueza CBD, Couto CC, Mocellin MC, Lamarca F, Saint'Pierre TD, Freitas Silva O, Ribas SA
abstract_snippet: Systematic review and meta-analysis: daily consumption may be unsafe due to As Cd Cu Co methyl-Hg Zn across infant formulas follow-up formulas and products for young children.

title: Infant exposure to trace elements in breast milk, infant formulas and complementary foods from southern China
abstract_snippet: Chinese study of 61 breast milk + 54 formula + 90 complementary food samples for Co Cr Cu Se Zn As Cd Ni Pb. 14.8-55.6% of commercial formulas contained Cr Cu or Se below reference values.
column16: Elsevier closed access; Science of the Total Environment (PMID 35690194)

title: Trace elements in commercially available infant formulas in Iran: Determination and estimation of health risks
abstract_snippet: As Cd Cr Cu Ni Pb measured in Iranian infant formulas. Mean Cr=0.398 mg/kg Pb=0.285 mg/kg. Health quotients exceeded thresholds for Cr Ni Pb in 61-89% of formulas. Carcinogenic risk from Cd Cr Ni.

title: Determination of Lead, Cadmium and Arsenic in Infant Formula in the Lebanese Market
authors: Elaridi J, Dimassi H, Al Yamani O, Estephan M, Hassan HF
abstract_snippet: ICP-MS analysis of Pb Cd and As in infant formula samples from Lebanese market. No abstract in metadata. Food Control 2021.

title: Determination of Aluminum, Chromium, and Barium Concentrations in Infant Formula Marketed in Lebanon
abstract_snippet: 78 infant formula samples from 39 Lebanese brands. All had Al and Ba; Cr detected in 95% of brands. Mean: Al=1.54 ug/g Ba=0.256 ug/g Cr=0.168 ug/g. Soy-based formulas higher in Al.
notes: Closed access (PMID 32971540); covers Al + Cr in formula

title: Assessment of Aluminum via Baby Foods Consumption in Turkey: Estimated Early-Life Dietary Exposure and Target Hazard Quotient
abstract_snippet: ICP-MS on 64 baby foods in 348 infants. Infant formula Al 718-6987 ug/kg; biscuits 1803-15479 ug/kg. Exposure 8.02-4.03 ug/kg BW/day. THQ 10-20 suggesting health concern.

title: Simultaneous Determination of Arsenic, Cadmium, Mercury, and Lead in Raw Ingredients, Nutritional Products, and Infant Formula by ICP-MS
abstract_snippet: ICP-MS method for As Cd Hg Pb in infant formula and nutritional products. Overall precision 2-14% RSD across analyte concentrations. Validation meets accuracy and linearity requirements.
notes: OUP returned 403; Unpaywall confirms closed. Method validation paper (year<2020)

title: Nutrient exploration and heavy metal risk assessment of baby milk and infant formulae sold within Umuahia metropolis, Nigeria
authors: Mgbemena MN, Okwunodulu IN, Okwunodulu FU, Onuchi Mac-Kalunta M, Okorie-Chukwuemeka H
abstract_snippet: 8 baby milk + 12 infant formula samples; only cadmium and chromium posed health risk in some Baby Milk samples. Most nutrients adequate.

title: Concentrations of Heavy Metals in Processed Baby Foods and Infant Formulas Worldwide: A Scoping Review
authors: Collado-Lopez S, Rodriguez Hernandez MF, Mariscal-Moreno RM et al.
abstract_snippet: Global evidence synthesis: Pb Cd As detected in >60% of baby foods. Rice products highest As. Significant risks for infants 6+ months from rice products and stage 1/2 formulas.

title: Monte Carlo simulation approach for health risk analysis of heavy metals' contamination in infant formula and food on the Iranian market
authors: Rahati S, Asadi Touranlou F, Afshari A, Hashemi M, Orooji A, Tavakoly Sany SB
journal: Journal of Health Population and Nutrition
abstract_snippet: 80 infant formula + 27 complementary food samples; Al Co Cr Cu Fe Zn exceeded FAO/WHO standards. Non-cancer HQ exceeded safety for all ages. Cancer risk 9.55e-5 to 3.57e-4.

title: Human Milk as a Biomonitor of Toxic Metal Exposure: Sources, Transfer Mechanisms, and Implications for Infant Health - A Review
abstract_snippet: Review of toxic metal occurrence in human milk including lead (approx 2-5 ug/L) cadmium mercury arsenic chromium aluminum. Benefits of breastfeeding outweigh risks despite contamination.

title: Urinary biomarkers of exposure to toxic and essential elements: A comparison of infants fed with human milk or formula
abstract_snippet: 462 infants; formula-fed had 5.15x higher urinary arsenic vs breastfed. Molybdenum and selenium elevated in formula-fed; uranium and cobalt lower.

title: Toxic Metals and Metalloids in Infant Formulas Marketed in Brazil, and Child Health Risks According to the Target Hazard Quotients and Target Cancer Risk
journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract_snippet: ICP-MS in Brazilian formula: Al 0.432-1.241 mg/kg; As 0.012-0.034 mg/kg; Sn 0.007-0.095 mg/kg; Hg Pb U also measured. As posed significant THQ concerns.

title: Essential and non-essential element concentrations in human milk samples and the assessment of infants' exposure
abstract_snippet: 30 Polish mothers' milk samples; 18 elements measured. Sn notably elevated at 5.67 ug/L vs WHO ~1.0 ug/L. Cd correlated with salty snack consumption.

title: Toxic elements in baby and young children's foods in the US and correlation to ingredients
journal: Food Additives and Contaminants Part B
abstract_snippet: 566 ready-to-eat baby foods for As Cd Hg Pb thallium. As associated with rice; Pb with root vegetables; thallium with brassica. Arsenic speciation and MeHg subsets analyzed.
